title: Orchestrator-runtime handshake and ownership catalog
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures a pragmatic, implementation-focused handshake contract between the control-plane orchestrator ("Orchestrator") and runtime adapters (GPU pools, sidecars, regional runtimes). It also proposes a compact ownership catalog: who owns which surface, the oncall implications, and a migration checklist for rolling orchestration changes multi-region.

Why this exists (short):
- There is ambiguity in runtime adapter responsibilities (health vs capacity vs feature flags).
- Multi-region failover behavior has been codified in multiple RFCs but not in a single, actionable owner map.
- We need a small, machine-readableish contract that teams can implement quickly.

Scope:
- Covers request routing, readiness/health semantics, cache/kv handshake, and circuit-breaker fallback policies.
- Focus is on the Orchestrator <-> Runtime Adapter boundary plus API Gateway edge responsibilities where relevant.
- Out of scope: detailed kernel selection logic, per-model quantization choices, and tenant billing.

1) High-level handshake summary (plain english)
- Orchestrator owns policy decisions: route selection (by latency/cost/tier), rollout signals, and global fallback rules.
- Runtime Adapter owns execution: accepting requests, reporting capacity/pressure, local fallbacks (eg. degraded quantized model), and health signals.
- API Gateway owns edge-related concerns: auth, per-tenant rate limiting, and transforming external requests into internal Orchestrator route candidates.

2) Contract (v1) — minimal fields exchanged (proto/http-json)
- Adapter -> Orchestrator: POST /adapter/register {adapter_id, region, capabilities:[streaming,kv-cache,quantized-8bit], capacity_score, max_batch_tokens, maintenance_window?} 
- Orchestrator -> Adapter: POST /adapter/{id}/deploy {model_id, model_variant, rollout_id, priority_score, expected_qos_ms, route_id} 
- Adapter -> Orchestrator: PUT /adapter/{id}/status {uptime_pct, ready:bool, healthy:bool, backlog_length, avg_latency_ms, last_kv_prefill_ts} 
- Orchestrator -> Adapter: GET /adapter/{id}/config  (returns runtime knobs: batch_window_ms, max_concurrent_requests, enable_prefix_cache)
- Liveness vs Readiness: adapter should expose both. Readiness=false => do not route new traffic; Liveness=false => node needs restart.

3) Health semantics (opinionated)
- Shallow health (liveness): process alive, event loop responsive. Adapter must return within 100ms. Liveness=false triggers immediate k8s restart or equivalent.
- Readiness: model loaded, KV cache warm enough (optional threshold), batch pipeline primed. Readiness=false => orchestrator drains traffic and marks adapter as 'standby'.
- Degraded: ready=true, healthy=false -> accept low-priority traffic only (configurable per-route).

4) Capacity scoring and routing hints
- Adapter reports capacity_score in 0..100. Orchestrator uses weighted capacity + latency to pick candidate set.
- Soft failover: if chosen adapter backlog_length > threshold OR avg_latency_ms > expected_qos_ms*1.5 -> orchestrator attempts alternate candidate.
- Hard failover: readiness=false or region outage -> immediate reroute.

5) Cache/KV prefill handshake
- When orchestrator routes a request with model-prefix X and adapter reports prefilling capability, orchestrator may send a prefill request: POST /adapter/{id}/kv/prefill {prefix_hash, tokens_to_prefill, ttl_ms}. Adapter replies with estimate. Prefill is best-effort; failures are logged but do not block routing.

6) API Gateway responsibilities (edge)
- Authenticate -> Enforce per-tenant quotas -> Attach tenant headers and route candidates to Orchestrator.
- Do not perform deep routing decisions based on load — Gateway only ranks things it can observe (cold starts, region proximity). Final routing decision is in Orchestrator.

7) Multi-region routing policy (matrix)
- Primary region = tenant preference or lowest latency region. Replica region used when: region outage OR latency > threshold for > 10s OR cost-threshold policy.
- Priority order: pinned-region > region-preference > low-latency > cheapest-available.
- Data residency pin overrides fallback unless policy allows cross-region processing (explicit tenant opt-in).

8) Failure modes and graceful degradation patterns
- Warm fallback: route to quantized/cheaper model variant in the same adapter pool when capacity constrained. Adapter should advertise available_variants. Orchestrator prefers same pool fallback to avoid cross-region data movement.
- Regional spillover: if region is at 95% capacity and backlog rising, orchestrator gradually shifts new traffic to backup region with traffic drain windows (configurable per rollout).
- API Gateway backpressure: when Orchestrator signals cluster-wide overload, Gateway should 503-fast-fail for new requests under 'best-effort' routes and allow reserved-tier routes to continue.

9) Ownership catalog (compact table)
Service | Primary owner | Backup owner | Oncall implications
API Gateway | eng-platform-gateway (team lead: Diego Ramos) | eng-platform-sre (backup: Hannah Lee) | Gateways own auth bugs, rate-limit blowups, and edge DDOS responses
Orchestrator core | eng-platform-orchestration (lead: Marcus Chen) | eng-platform-infra | Oncall must be able to toggle regional policies and initiate global fallbacks
Runtime Adapter fleet (regional) | eng-runtime-ops (lead: S. Kim) | eng-platform-infra | Adapters own model loading regressions, memory leaks, and adapter-specific circuit breakers
Observability (tracing/metrics) | eng-observability | eng-platform-infra | Own dashboards and alerting on route SLOs, token cost anomalies

10) Runbook snippets (for oncall)
- If region latency spikes: check adapter backpressure metrics -> run 'drain' on overloaded adapters -> enable regional spillover if drain does not reduce latency within 2 mins.
- If orchestrator process is healthy but routing decisions are failing: inspect policy cache and rollout flags -> if inconsistency, toggle rollout to previous stable id and force sync to adapters.

11) Rollout checklist (orchestrator policy change)
- Write policy and unit tests (policy simulator)
- Deploy to staging, run synthetic traffic against adapters across regions
- Canary in one low-traffic region for 2 hours -> measure 99th p50/p95/p99 for token latency and cost deltas
- Ramp using gradual traffic percentage with automatic rollback on SLO breach
- Communicate to runtime-ops and gateway teams 24h before major rollout

12) Migration notes (how to move adapter ownership or introduce a new adapter type)
- New adapter registers with a 'training' tag and capacity_score=0 by default
- Orchestrator includes adapter in canary routes only when operator flips 'enable_training_adapters' flag and verifies end-to-end metrics for 6 hours
- To change primary owner: run change-of-responsibility doc + 2-week shadowing with backup owner oncall

13) Open questions / TODOs
- Should adapters expose per-model memory footprints to allow smarter packing decisions? (tradeoff: privacy/leak risk)
- Do we need a versioned contract schema (v1, v2) published in a registry? Pro: safer migrations. Con: more infra.
- What is the canonical source of truth for region capacity? Orchestrator maintains a cache now; consider central capacity service.

14) References and links
- Confluence: Orchestrator Design (linked above)
- RFC-PLAT-112: Regional Failover Patterns
- GH-PR-2891: adapter-sidecar: health and prefill implementation

Appendix: quick ascii flow (request path)
Client -> API Gateway (auth, tenant attach) -> Orchestrator (rank candidates) -> Adapter A (accept) -> Adapter A executes -> returns stream/response -> Orchestrator logs traces -> Gateway returns to client

Notes to self / rough ideas: 
- Could we push a tiny langchain-style local cache in API Gateway to reduce cold-starts for small latencies? Maybe only for ephemeral session keys.
- Consider adding a "graceful_degradation_profile" in the deploy call so adapters can switch to that profile locally during emergencies.

Last updated notes:
- 2025-09-17 initial draft
- 2025-10-05 added KV prefill semantics and capacity scoring rules
- 2025-11-02 added ownership table and runbook snippets
